questions.question: Which one of the following countries is NOT a member of ASEAN?
questions.solution:

questions.question: Where is the origin of Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers situated respectively?
questions.solution:
​The correct answer is __**Uttarakhand and Tibet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The river Ganga originates from Devprayag in Uttarakhand at the confluence of the rivers Alaknanda and Bhagirathi.
 
• The river Brahmaputra originates from the Angsi Glacier in Burang County, Tibet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Ganga River__: 

 __
 
• The Ganges rises in the southern Great Himalayas on the Indian side of the border with the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.
 
• Its five major streams—the Bhagirathi, the Alaknanda, the Mandakini, the Dhauliganga, and the Pindar—all rise in the mountainous region of northern Uttarakhand state.
 
• Among them, the two main streams are the Alaknanda (the longer of the two), which rises about 30 miles (50 km) north of the Himalayan peak of Nanda Devi, and the Bhagirathi, which rises about 10,000 feet (3,000 m). above sea level in a subglacial meltwater cave at the base of a Himalayan glacier known as Gangotri.
 
• Gangotri itself is a holy place for Hindu pilgrimage. However, the original source of the Ganges is believed to be Gaumukh, about 13 miles (21 km) southeast of Gangotri.
 
 
 
• Brahmaputra River__: 
 
 
• The source of the Brahmaputra is the Chemayungdung Glacier, which covers the Himalayan slopes about 60 miles (100 km) southeast of Mapam Lake in southwestern Tibet.
 
• The Kubi, Angasi, and Chemayungdung are the three major streams that originate there.
 
• From its source, the river runs in a generally easterly direction for about 700 miles (1,100 km) between the Great Himalayan Range in the south and the Kailas Range in the north.
 
• Throughout its upper course, the river is generally referred to as the Tsangpo ("purifier").
 
• It is also known by its Chinese name (Yarlung Zangbo) and other local Tibetan names.

questions.question: Upanishad Books are: ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**On philosophy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The Upanishads are late Vedic Sanskrit texts of religious teachings and ideas still revered in Hinduism.

 
 
• The Upanishads played an important role in the development of spiritual ideas in ancient India, marking a transition from Vedic ritualism to new ideas and institutions.
 
• Upanishad literally means ‘approaching and ​sitting near’ and the texts contain conversations between teachers and students.
 
• Often, ideas were presented through simple dialogues.
 
• The Upanishads were written over a time period ranging from **700 to 400 B.C.E**
 
• Upanishads focused on Spiritual enlightenment.
 
• Upanishad is derived from the words *upa (near) and shad (to sit).* It is derived from the concept of sitting near the feet of the teacher.
 
• More than 200 Upanishads have been discovered.
 
• Each Upanishad is associated with a certain Veda.
 
• There are 14 Upanishads which are most well known or most important – Katha, Kena, Isa, Mundaka, Prasna, Taittiriya, Chhandogya, Brihadaranyaka, Mandukya, Aitareya, Kaushitaki, Svetasvatara and Maitrayani.
 
• Upanishads are in the last section of any Vedas. Upanishads are a subcategory of a Veda.
 
• Upanishads is one of the 4 major text types of Vedas.
 
• Upanishads are texts on spiritual knowledge and philosophy.
 
• Upanishads originated from each branch of Vedas.
 
• Upanishads deals with the philosophical aspects of life.

questions.question: Atomic number is always equal to ______.
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Atomic number** is always equal to the **number of protons** present in the nucleus.
 
• However, if the atom has **no electrical charge** present in it, then the atomic number is **also **equal to the **number of electrons** present since the number of protons and electrons will be the same.

Electrons:

 
• 
 
Discovered by Sir J.J Thomson in the year 1897.

 
 
• Previously named as cathode rays as they were supposed to be emitted from the cathode.
 
• They are deflected towards the positive side.
 
• They have high kinetic energy.
 
• They are deflected by an electric and magnetic field.
 
• It has a negative charge of
 
• 
 
 charge=1.602×10⁻¹⁹ coulombs 

 mass={1over 1837}times 9.107times 10⁻²⁸g

 
Protons:

 
 
• Discovered by Goldstein.
 
• Depicted first as positive rays because it seemed to emerge from the anode.
 
• Mass of a proton is

 1.670 times 10⁻ ²⁴g

Charge=1.602times 10⁻¹⁹ coulombs​

Explanation:__

__
 
• Rutherford's discovery led to the discovery of nucleus.
 
• He found out that most of the mass of the nucleus is situated in its centre and contains the positively charged particles protons.
 
• The atom is otherwise empty and as electrons have negligible mass, the mass of an atom should be equal to the sum of mass of protons present in it.
 
• However, it was seen that in Helium, there are only two protons, so its mass should be twice the mass of each proton = 2times 1.008 a.m.u.
 
• Experimental results revealed that it has a mass of 4.003a.m.u.
 
• Hence, it was concluded that the nucleus has particles containing no charge but mass almost equal to that of a proton.
 
• This was established by scientist James chadwick in 1932.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Rutherford's gold foil experiment: 

 
• He discovered the atomic nucleus and gave us an atomic model.
 
• He directed alpha particles towards a metal sheet.
 
• He saw that most of the alpha particles, which are positively charged particles, are not getting deflected.
 
• Most of the alpha particles emerged undeflected.
 
• 
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ef1a0df1376006491f1fb29083b5a28c3ee4c8084f5dfa8a7dec27c094d7386e.png] 

 
 
• Therefore, he concluded that most of the mass of the nucleus is situated in its centre and contains the positively charged particles protons.
 
• Electrons revolve around the nucleus in certain orbits.

questions.question:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are INCORRECT?

I. Alkenes are fairly unreactive.

II. Alkenes burn with blue flame.

III. Alkanes burn with yellow flame.
questions.solution:
• **Alkenes**, in organic chemistry, are the **unsaturated hydrocarbons** which at least contain one carbon-carbon double bond. They are **more reactive than alkanes**, burn with a **sooty and smoky flame which is yellow in color.** This indicates incomplete combustion due to the presence of carbon-carbon double bond.
 
• **Alkanes** are the **saturated hydrocarbons** and burn with a **blue flame**.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act gave constitutional recognition to the Panchayats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**73rd Constitutional Amendment Act**__.

 
• The **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992** gave constitutional recognition to the Panchayats by adding a **new schedule 11** and **new part IX** to the Indian Constitution.
 
• The **74th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992** gave constitutional recognition to the **Municipalities** by adding a **new schedule 12** and **new part IX-A** to the Indian Constitution.
 
• The **Constitution (75th Amendment) Act 1994 **provides for setting up of State-level Rent Tribunals to exclude the jurisdiction of all courts, except that of the Supreme Court, under Article 136 of the Constitution.
 
• The **Constitution** (**72nd Amendment**) **Ac****t**,** 1992** to make temporary provision for the determination of the number of seats reserved for the Scheduled Tribes in the State assembly of Tripura, until the re-adjustment of seats is made on the basis of the first census after the year 2000 under article 170 of the Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT included in the excretory system of human being?
questions.solution:
• The **excretory system** in a human body is responsible for the removal of unnecessary and excess materials from the body fluids to prevent the body from any damage and to help maintain the internal chemical homeostasis.
 
• It comprises of **ureters**, **kidneys**, **urinary bladder**, and **urethra**.

questions.question: By which process substance like carbon dioxide or oxygen can move across the cell membrane?
questions.solution:
• **Diffusion** is the process by which substance like carbon dioxide or oxygen can move across the cell membrane.
 
• **Plasmolysis** is the process during which the cells lose water in a hypertonic solution.
 
• **Sedimentation** is the process of settling out of the particles from the suspension in water to form sediment.
 
• **Transpiration** is a process through which water moves through a plant and evaporates from its aerial parts.

questions.question: Researchers from Columbia University Medical Centre in United States of America have converted which of the following into the world’s smallest data recorder?
questions.solution:
• Researchers from **Columbia University Medical Centre** in the United States of America have converted a **natural bacterial immune system** into the world’s smallest microscopic data recorder.
 
• They modified an ordinary laboratory strain of ubiquitous human gut microbe *Escherichiacoli* (E.Coli), a bacterium which enabled it to record the time-stamp events and their interactions with the environment.

questions.question: As per RBI in October 2017, Gross Non-Performing Assets (GNPA) ratio for NBFCs increased to what percentage till March 2017?

• Due to the deterioration in the asset quality of **NBFCs**, the **GNPA ratio** increased from **4.5% in 2016 to 5.0% in 2017.**
 
• Still, there asset quality remained better than that of the banks. The **GNPA ratio** for **scheduledcommercial banks** increased from **8.4% to 9.6%**.

questions.question: A Sonar of a ship sends sounds waves of speed 1000 m/s. These waves are reflected back by the ocean floor in 2 seconds. Find the depth (in m) of the ocean floor.
questions.solution:
__Given__:-

Speed of sound waves = 1000m/s

Total time (time to go + time to come back) of waves = 2sec (1sec each)

Thus, depth (distance) of the ocean floor = speed × time = 1000 × 1 = 1000m

questions.question: If the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the earth is g, then the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of a planet whose mass is same as that of earth and radius is half as that of the earth is __________.
questions.solution:
• g=(GM)/(R²)
 
• **g **= acceleration due to gravity; **G **= universal gravitational constant; **M **= mass; **R **= distance (radius)
 
• Since ‘G’ is constant, the ‘**acceleration due to gravity**’ depends on ‘**mass**’ and ‘**radius**’. Now it is given that ‘mass’ is same, therefore now the only factor on which the ‘acceleration due to gravity’ depends is ‘radius’.

As we can see from the formula that, ‘radius’ is inversely proportional to ‘g’, thus if ‘radius’ is decreasing, ‘g’ will increase. Also, since there is a power of 2, therefore the ‘g’ will increase by 4 times.

questions.question: The objective of __________ is to make India a global information technology superpower.
